reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When building models that make binary decisions, researchers often need a way to turn any continuous measurement into a probability between zero and one. Linear functions fail because they grow without bound, producing nonsensical values outside this range. Pierre François Verhulst faced a similar problem studying population growth, leading him to propose a bounded curve.

By mapping the entire real line through an exponential transformation, the logistic function compresses extreme positive values toward one and extreme negative values toward zero. The central transition becomes steeper as the parameter increases, creating a smooth switch. Examining this curve reveals how the math guarantees outputs strictly within the unit interval.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function squashes any real number into the range between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness and midpoint to see how the S-curve responds.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness and midpoint sliders to reshape the sigmoid curve. Move the marker to inspect the output and slope at any input coordinate.
